newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-ITALY'S KOSTNER IS WARY AFTER WIN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ITALY'S KOSTNER IS WARY AFTER WIN.

text.p: Italy's Isolde Kostner, completing a hat-trick of wins on the Olimpia delle Tofane piste, won an Alpine skiing super-giant slalom on Saturday for her second victory in two days.

The super-G world champion, whose World Cup wins had previously been limited to downhills, beat Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg and Germany's Katja Seizinger into second and third places with a time of one minute 17.04 seconds.
Wiberg -- the slalom, overall and super-G World Cup leader -- clocked 1:17.14 and Seizinger, her big rival, 1:17.24.

The victory was the 21-year-old Kostner's third at Cortina in three races here -- she won in the smart Italian resort last season and shared the glory in Friday's downhill after clocking the same time as Switzerland's Heidi Zurbriggen.
It was the fourth World Cup win of her career.
"This win is important for me because it is on the course that I really like and in front of all my family here," said the Italian whose home is not far away in Val Gardena.

But she cautioned that although her win on Friday had made her more relaxed, her success could have a negative effect by increasing expectations in Italy ahead of the world championships on home snow in Sestriere next month.

"I can imagine the people getting even more excited now and we have to be relaxed to handle the pressure," said Kostner. "I have a lot of experience in medal events but I can imagine that things will be crazy in Sestriere. It is going to be a madhouse."
Itay's in-form women's team are carrying more than their usual share of the nation's expectations because of the absence for most of the season of men's superstar Alberto Tomba.
The country's daily Gazzetta dello Sport newspaper ran a headline on Saturday, after the downhill, declaring that "Kostner can feel the world championships in her pocket".
"I am getting the same feeling that I had last year before we went to Sierra Nevada for the world championships," said Stefan Holzer, Kostner's ski technician.
"At that time her success in Cortina was fundamental because it reassured her about the work we had done."
The Italian women have now won four out of the last five races, with Deborah Compagnoni taking back-to-back giant slalom wins at the German resort of Zwiesel last week.
World champion and double Olympic gold medallist Compagnoni will be in action again on Sunday in a giant here.
On Saturday, the leading trio started one after the other, with Kostner sixth out of the hut ahead of Seizinger, who has yet to win a super-G this season, and Wiberg -- who has won two.

"I made a mistake yesterday in being too aggressive," said Wiberg, who has won every discipline in the World Cup except the downhill and had hoped to rectify that in Cortina but finished only seventh.
"I put too much pressure on myself and it was a big lesson for me again. I learned a lot yesterday."
The Swede said she had been far more relaxed in the super-G and was happy with her continuing good form.
Seizinger, who had hoped to rein in Wiberg in the overall standings, commented ironically that she seemed to have a season ticket on third places but was otherwise happy.
Wiberg leads the overall World Cup with 1,189 points to Seizinger's 865. She also leads the super-G standings with 389 points, ahead of Germany's Hilde Gerg on 330.
